pub assume_specification<T: core::default::Default, E>[ Result::<T, E>::unwrap_or_default ](
    result: Result<T, E>,
) -> (res: T)
    ensures
        result is Ok ==> res == result->Ok_0,
        result is Err ==> T::default.ensures((), res),
;
candidates.rationale: The alias resolves to Result<T, E>; the source returns the Ok payload or calls Default::default, both expressible using existing Result and callable-contract vocabulary.
risks: The Err branch is only as informative as T::default's specification.
The contract describes normal return and does not exclude effects or panics from Default or destructors.

pub assume_specification<T, E, F: FnOnce(E) -> T>[ Result::<T, E>::unwrap_or_else ](
    result: Result<T, E>,
    op: F,
) -> (res: T)
    requires
        result is Err ==> op.requires((result->Err_0,)),
    ensures
        result is Ok ==> res == result->Ok_0,
        result is Err ==> op.ensures((result->Err_0,), res),
;
candidates.rationale: The source branches only on the materialized Result, returning its Ok payload or invoking op on its Err payload; FnOnce requires/ensures captures this exactly.
risks: Usefulness on the Err branch depends on the closure having a usable contract.
The contract does not assert termination or absence of panic.

pub assume_specification<T, E>[ Result::<T, E>::unwrap_unchecked ](
    result: Result<T, E>,
) -> (res: T)
    requires
        result is Ok,
    ensures
        res == result->Ok_0,
;
candidates.rationale: The source returns the Ok payload and declares Err usage undefined behavior, directly supporting the Ok precondition and payload equality.
risks: Calling the API on Err remains undefined behavior and is excluded by the precondition.
